t: Spiritists believe in one God, in the immortality of the spirit, in reincarnation as the means of moral and material improvement, and in useful communication with spirits through mediums.
The doctrine rests on five works by Allan Kardec, the Spiritist Codification of 1857–1868, and has no priestly hierarchy: its basic unit is the Spiritist centre, a non-profit association.
Brazil has the most Spiritists, about 3.8 million in the census of 2010, and there the doctrine was banned by the penal code of 1890 until the code of 1940 ended the prohibition.
dyk: Kardec’s own account of table-turning is that, to obtain longer answers, he had the table knock a number of times for each letter of the alphabet; asked what it was, the being that answered declared itself a spirit.
ev: The events at the home of the Fox sisters in Hydesville begin on 31 March; many Spiritists mark the date as the first milestone of modern mediumistic manifestations
Kardec publishes The Spirits’ Book on 18 April and coins the term spiritisme
Spiritism reaches Brazil in the 1860s; the Brazilian Spiritist Federation dates its arrival to this year
Kardec dies; Spiritism is said to have gained 7 million followers since 1857
The Brazilian Spiritist Federation is founded in Rio de Janeiro on 2 January
Brazil’s penal code bans the practice of Spiritism, punishing it with up to six months in prison
Brazil’s penal code of 1940 ends the official prohibition of Spiritism
The International Spiritist Council is constituted in Madrid on 28 November

f.origin: France, in the mid-19th century, with the publication of The Spirits’ Book in 1857 by Hippolyte Léon Denizard Rivail, writing as Allan Kardec, after he observed table-turning and the spiritualist currents of Europe and the United States.
f.founder: Allan Kardec (Hippolyte Léon Denizard Rivail), a French writer and educator, who coined the term spiritisme in 1857 and directed the Revue Spirite until his death in 1869.
f.scriptures: The Spiritist Codification, five basic works by Kardec published between 1857 and 1868: The Spirits’ Book, The Mediums’ Book, The Gospel According to Spiritism, Heaven and Hell, and The Genesis, with complementary works such as What is Spiritism?, the Spiritist Review and Posthumous Works.
f.followers: About 13 million worldwide according to data from 2005, in 36 countries according to the International Spiritist Council; about 3.8 million in Brazil in the census of 2010, the country with the most followers.
